p2-q1.actual: GET /api/leads now takes real query params applied server-side before the response is built: `nation` (exact match vs the row's `nation` field), `haf` (1/true or 0/false vs the boolean `haf` field), and `bookingUrl` (substring match vs the row's `bookingUrl`, e.g. a platform hostname). Verified against the live dev API (71,733 real leads in the collection) with a throwaway platform account: nation=England on the loaded cache window returned 200 items out of a filtered total of 4,949, and every returned row genuinely had nation=England; bookingUrl=www.ticketsource.co.uk returned exactly 7 rows, all with that host in their bookingUrl. Because this dev server's in-memory cache is capped (LEADS_CACHE_MAX=5000, unrelated pre-existing cost control, newest-first) it happened to hold no Wales/haf:true rows at the moment of the live-HTTP test, even though Firestore confirms 2,701 Wales and 5,859 haf:true leads exist in the full collection — so nation=Wales/haf=true returned 0/0 over HTTP, which would misread as broken filtering. Proved it isn't: pulled 1,000 real Wales/haf:true docs straight from Firestore (bypassing the cache) and ran the exact same filterRows() predicate against them directly — nation=wales matched 511/511 correctly, haf=true matched 517/517, haf=false matched 483/483 (all haf!==true), and nation=wales AND haf=true matched 28/28. Before this fix every one of nation/haf/bookingUrl was silently ignored and the full (capped) list was always returned regardless of query params.
p2-q1.notes: The exclusion of Wales/haf:true from the live-HTTP sample is a side effect of the PRE-EXISTING CACHE_MAX=5000 cap (newest-first import order), not of this fix — raising LEADS_CACHE_MAX would need a dev-server restart, which was avoided per standing instruction not to interrupt running dev servers unannounced. The filter predicate itself was proven correct against real matching rows independent of the cache window (see actual). server/src/routes/leads.ts.

p2-r9.actual: GET /api/leads is the specific b36 item this step names (71,718→71,733 docs today; previously 39,286 rows unpaged, full read every call, no limit/cursor param). It now supports the same `?limit=&cursor=` -> `{ items in `leads`, total, nextCursor }` pagination idiom already used by hub questions.ts/learningHub.ts. Verified live: walking the real endpoint in pages of 25 (limit=25&cursor=<offset>) covered all 5,000 rows in the current cache window across 200 pages, with distinct ids collected across pages summing to exactly the reported `total` (5,000) — pages genuinely partition the same set the old unpaged call returned, none missing, none duplicated. Before/after size and time on THIS server: unfiltered/unpaged (old default shape) = 4,831,986 bytes / 513ms for 5,000 rows; filtered (nation=Wales&haf=true) + paged (limit=25) = 121 bytes / 152ms for 0 matching rows in this cache window, and nation=England + limit=200 = 198,229 bytes / 225ms for 200 of 4,949 matching rows — both a large multiple smaller than the 4.8MB unfiltered response. A single request can no longer return the whole unbounded 71,733-doc collection: the cache itself stays capped at CACHE_MAX (5,000, pre-existing), and within that a paged request is further capped per page (limit clamped to <=CACHE_MAX, default 500).
p2-r9.notes: At true full-collection scale (71,733 docs) the historical failure mode (132.6s / 62MB unpaged) is now impossible from this route regardless of cache size, because pagination is enforced on top of whatever the cache holds and the cache itself is already capped. The dev database's real lead volume (71,733) was large enough to demonstrate the fix directly — no seeding needed.
p2-r9.evidence: server/src/routes/leads.ts (GET / pagination + filterRows); features/platform/LeadsApp.tsx (loadAllPages walks pages of 2000 instead of trusting one response); throwaway verification scripts (deleted after the run)
